forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 22→23%. Late-June 2026 saw the US government formally gate frontier access: Anthropic's 'Mythos 5' was re-authorised for ~100 trusted US organisations and OpenAI began previewing GPT-5.6 'Sol' to government-vetted partners (26 June). Rising capability and institutional-concern signals, but the resolution bar is still unmet — no lab has declared 'AGI' and there is no 3+ researcher convergence. Small upward nudge.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: near-term insider predictions of a transformative technology arriving within a fixed ~3.5-year window, where insiders carry optimism incentives. Such forecasts resolve YES well under half the time; base ~15-20%.

factors_up.factor: Lab leadership timelines (Amodei ~2026-2027, Altman within the term) sit inside the window
Move to government-gated frontier access signals capability advancing fast enough to prompt federal control

factors_down.factor: Resolution bar (clean credible declaration or 3+ researchers) remains unmet and definitionally contested
General-agent benchmarks (e.g. ARC-AGI-3) still show frontier models near zero, underscoring remaining gaps

key_uncertainties: Whether any major lab will formally declare 'AGI' rather than avoiding the term
Whether 3+ leading researchers would publicly converge on 'AGI achieved' before 2030
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible lab announces AGI or 3+ leading researchers state it is achieved
Revise DOWN if frontier progress visibly plateaus or labs explicitly disavow near-term AGI

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 25%. No fresh sector-specific data point in the last few days; the McKinsey/Bain/BCG/Deloitte AI-driven headcount reductions (~10% at McKinsey) remain the key evidence. A ≥33% revenue or employment decline attributed primarily to AI by end-2030 stays a high bar with difficult clean attribution against a noisy macro backdrop.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: incumbent professional-services sectors facing a major technology shock losing ≥33% of value/employment within ~6 years. Historically rare on that timescale; base ~10-15%.

factors_up.factor: Visible AI-driven layoffs across major consultancies and AI-native boutique competition
Core deliverables (slide-making, research synthesis, modelling) are highly automatable

factors_down.factor: Clean attribution of ≥33% decline 'primarily to AI' is analytically demanding
Consultancies are repositioning toward AI-transformation advisory, cushioning revenue

key_uncertainties: Whether 2+ credible analyses will attribute a ≥33% decline primarily to AI
Whether revenue falls as sharply as headcount, or firms pivot to AI advisory work
update_triggers: Revise UP if credible analyses report consultancy revenue/employment down sharply on AI
Revise DOWN if the sector stabilises or grows via AI-transformation mandates

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 6%. PollCheck's 7-poll average (25 June) has Reform UK on 26.4%, Labour 19.9% and the Conservatives 19.6% — Labour edging back ahead of the Tories for second but still well behind a durable Reform lead. With the next GE not due until 2029 recovery is possible, but Labour-largest remains unlikely on current standings.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: governing party polling third, ~6-7pp behind the leader at roughly mid-term, going on to win most seats at the next election. Uncommon but not unprecedented over a multi-year runway; base ~10-15%.

factors_up.factor: ~3 years to the election allows time for recovery and incumbency advantages
FPTP can convert a modest Labour recovery into most seats given fragmented opposition

factors_down.factor: Durable Reform UK lead (~26%) with Labour stuck around 19-20%
Persistently weak PM approval and governing-party drag

key_uncertainties: Whether the Reform UK surge proves durable to the next election
How FPTP translates a fragmented four/five-party vote into seats
update_triggers: Revise UP if Labour recovers to within a few points of the lead or moves into first
Revise DOWN if Reform's lead widens or Labour support erodes further

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 82→83%. Continued broad-based frontier progress (OpenAI GPT-5.5 and limited GPT-5.6 'Sol', Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8/Mythos 5, Google Gemini 3.5) plus the move to government-gated access are consistent with a capability trajectory that comfortably fits a ~9-year horizon. Minor upward adjustment to the medium-term path.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: expert/community forecasts for transformative AI within a ~9-10 year horizon. Aggregators and many researchers place this above 50%; base ~55-70%.

factors_up.factor: Sustained rapid scaling and capability gains across multiple labs
Long runway (to 2035) absorbs plausible slowdowns and still clears the bar

factors_down.factor: Definitional/resolution ambiguity could delay a clean 'AGI achieved' verdict
Possible scaling plateaus, compute/energy or regulatory constraints

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling and algorithmic progress continue without a multi-year plateau
Whether the 'AGI' resolution bar is met cleanly even if capabilities are very high
update_triggers: Revise UP if labs declare AGI or near-AGI milestones are widely acknowledged
Revise DOWN if frontier progress stalls or hard compute/regulatory limits bite

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 7%. AEI's 26 June China-Taiwan update and prediction markets (Polymarket ~3% by 30 June) continue to judge a near-term blockade or invasion unlikely; Beijing favours grey-zone coercion (a mid-June maritime law-enforcement operation east of the island) and the PLA has not adopted the joint-training model needed for a large-scale operation. Multi-year tail risk keeps this non-trivial.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: great-power initiation of a major amphibious blockade/invasion against a defended island within a ~3.5-year window, absent active mobilisation. Very low; base ~3-6%.

factors_up.factor: Continued PLA exercises rehearsing blockade scenarios and sustained pressure
Structural risk of miscalculation around elections or external shocks

factors_down.factor: No verifiable large-scale mobilisation; assessments see no fixed timeline
Enormous economic and military cost; PLA logistical/training gaps

key_uncertainties: Whether grey-zone pressure escalates into a >72hr blockade
How external events (US politics, regional crises) shift Beijing's calculus
update_triggers: Revise UP on verifiable large-scale mobilisation or amphibious build-up
Revise DOWN if cross-strait tensions ease or deterrence visibly strengthens

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 1%. ONS reported CPI at 2.8% in the 12 months to May 2026 (released 17 June), unchanged from April, with services and transport inflation firm. June data lands 22 July; with only ~5-6 monthly prints left to be published before January 2027 and inflation running well above target, a sub-2.0% reading is highly improbable.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: a ~1.0+pp drop in the headline annual CPI rate to below 2.0% within ~6 months from a starting point of 2.8% with firm services inflation. Rare absent a demand shock; base <5%.

factors_up.factor: Possible sharp energy/food disinflation or an unexpected demand shock

factors_down.factor: CPI stuck at 2.8% with sticky services and transport inflation
Few remaining monthly prints before the deadline

key_uncertainties: Whether an unforeseen energy-price collapse drags the headline rate down quickly
The path of services inflation over the next few prints
update_triggers: Revise UP if a monthly CPI print drops sharply toward 2%
Revise DOWN (toward floor) as each remaining print confirms above-target inflation

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 90→91%. Tracking continues to strengthen: best US first-day pre-sales in five years (>$40M) and a projected ~$250M domestic opening — the biggest debut since No Way Home — ahead of the 31 July release. Five months of runway to 31 December make $1.5B worldwide the most likely outcome, though it remains an elite threshold only a handful of films clear.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: MCU/Spider-Man tentpoles with a major opening clearing $1.5B worldwide. Several recent franchise entries have, but it is still an elite tier; base ~50-60% for this class, lifted by exceptional tracking.

factors_up.factor: Record-setting pre-sales and ~$250M projected domestic opening
Strong MCU/Spider-Man franchise pull and five months of runway

factors_down.factor: $1.5B is an elite threshold sensitive to legs and China/international performance
Reviews/word-of-mouth and competition could compress the multiplier

key_uncertainties: Actual opening magnitude and international/China contribution
update_triggers: Revise UP after a record opening weekend confirms tracking
Revise DOWN if the opening underwhelms or legs are weak

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 99%. Anthropic disclosed a ~$47B run-rate in mid-May 2026 and OpenAI is at ~$25B as of June; the combined gross run-rate (~$72B) already brackets the $70B threshold and both are still growing fast. A combined Q4 2026 figure above $70B is near-certain even allowing for gross-vs-net definitional disputes.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: hyper-growth AI firms sustaining run-rate trajectories over two further quarters. With the combined figure already near the threshold, conditional base rate is very high; ~95%+.

factors_up.factor: Anthropic ~$47B and OpenAI ~$25B run-rates already sum near/above $70B
Both firms still growing rapidly through H2 2026

factors_down.factor: Gross-vs-net ARR definitional disputes could shave reported figures
Reporting timing/availability of clean Q4 2026 ARR figures

key_uncertainties: Which ARR definition (gross vs net) credible reporting uses at resolution
Availability of comparable Q4 2026 figures for both firms
update_triggers: Revise DOWN only if growth sharply reverses or reporting adopts a much stricter net basis

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 38%. No new macro release in the last few days; the OBR's March 2026 path (medium-term productivity ~1%, AI adding ~0.2pp by the horizon, ~0.5% labour-supply growth) leaves the decade-average near the 1.5% threshold — a coin-toss tilted slightly below given recent productivity downgrades.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: UK decade-average real GDP growth exceeding 1.5%. The 2010s and early 2020s ran below; longer history is mixed. Base ~35-45%.

factors_up.factor: Potential AI-driven productivity acceleration later in the decade
Labour-supply growth (migration, participation) supports headline GDP

factors_down.factor: Persistent weak productivity and repeated OBR downgrades
Demographic ageing and fiscal drag weigh on trend growth

key_uncertainties: Whether AI delivers a measurable productivity uplift within the decade
The path of labour-supply growth and net migration policy
update_triggers: Revise UP if productivity data or OBR projections improve materially
Revise DOWN on further productivity downgrades or recession
